rich_summary: After threatening Sita, the enraged Ravana orders a band of grotesque demonesses to break her spirit. They drag the despairing princess to the Ashoka grove, a lush but prison-like garden where she will be guarded, threatened, and coaxed into yielding to him. Surrounded by terrifying watchers, Sita collapses in grief, remembering Rama and Lakshmana. Meanwhile, Rama—having slain the shape-shifting demon Maricha disguised as a deer—hurries back to the hermitage. Ominous signs fill the forest: jackals howl, beasts cry, and birds move ominously to his left. Realizing that Maricha’s dying imitation of his voice may have lured Lakshmana away, Rama fears a trap. When he finally sees Lakshmana returning alone, his anxiety deepens, and he reproaches him, convinced that terrible harm may have befallen Sita.

highlight_spans.why: Ravana’s furious command to the demonesses initiates Sita’s captivity and sets the emotional stakes for the coming search.
The transfer of Sita to the Ashoka grove establishes the central prison setting where much of her suffering and resistance will unfold.
The simile comparing Sita to a gazelle among tigresses captures her vulnerability and the emotional intensity of her isolation.
Rama’s encounter with ominous portents—howling jackals and fearful cries—signals the cosmic disturbance surrounding Sita’s abduction.

top_scenes.scene_text: Demonesses with monstrous forms drag the despairing Sita through flowering trees into the Ashoka grove while she collapses like a gazelle among tigresses.
Rama rushing through the dark forest after killing the demon-deer as jackals howl behind him and ominous birds circle overhead.
Rama grasping Lakshmana’s arm in the forest, anxiety on his face as he realizes Sita has been left alone among lurking demons.
